articles.title: LSU vs. Louisiana Tech: How to watch tonight's NCAA college football game, where to stream and more
articles.summary: Here's how to watch this weekend's LSU vs. Louisiana Tech NCAAF game.
articles.body:
As LSU's contentious battle with the SEC continues, the team still has a regular schedule to stick to, and in Week 2 of the NCAAF season, they'll face Louisiana Tech at home in Tiger Stadium this Saturday night. While Louisiana Tech enter the game as underdogs, they're riding high on an 80-6 win against Northwestern State in Week 1. (And you thought LSU's 51-10 win over Clemson last weekend was brutal…)

Here's what you need to know to watch the LSU vs. Louisiana Tech game, and take a look at the complete NCAAF schedule for Week 2.

Streaming: SECN+ , ESPN Unlimited, YouTube TV, Fubo, DIRECTV and more

When is the LSU vs. Louisiana Tech game?

LSU and Louisiana Tech play on Saturday, Sept. 12 at 7:30 p.m. ET.

What channel is the LSU vs. Louisiana Tech game on?

The LSU vs. Louisiana Tech game will air on SEC Network+. (SECN+ is complementary to SEC Network and part of your subscription with your cable, satellite, or streaming provider. Games on SECN+ are is only available digitally through ESPN Unlimited or by using a laptop, tablet or smartphone and authenticating with your cable login credentials if you have a plan that includes the SEC Network.)

How to watch LSU vs. Louisiana Tech without cable:

Saturday's LSU vs. Louisiana Tech game will stream on SECN+ which is included as part of ESPN Unlimited. ESPN Unlimited is included on live TV platforms like YouTube TV, Fubo, and DirecTV.

articles.title: Falcons Draft 2027: Way-Too-Early 2027 NFL Mock Draft 1.0
articles.summary: The Atlanta Falcons are in dire straits heading into the first week of the 2026 NFL season, as both projected starters at the quarterback position are out fo...
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons are in dire straits heading into the first week of the 2026 NFL season, as both projected starters at the quarterback position are out for the first game against the Pittsburgh Steelers . But that's not why we're here. Draft season is year-round nowadays, and the Falcons need multiple players throughout the roster if they're going to build a sturdy foundation to start competing for the division/conference sooner rather than later. Atlanta has done a great job not overextending in the short term, owning the most cap space in 2027, despite extending Drake London , Bijan Robinson , Kyle Pitts and Matthew Bergeron this offseason. However, even with the potential depth that money can bring, general manager Ian Cunningham and President Matt Ryan have to hit on the draft. So, we're going to get a jump on next year's draft by pinpointing seven picks in this way-too-early 2027 NFL mock draft.

Round 1, Pick 6: Darian Mensah, QB, Miami

I'm buying into the hype early. The former Duke transfer has come out of the gate firing, albeit against Stanford and Florida A&M. Mensah's 91.1% completion percentage is the second-best start to a college football season for any quarterback with 40+ attempts in the first two games, while his 271.7 Passer Efficiency Rating is the best. 41-of-45 for 653 yards, eight touchdowns, and zero interceptions. Miami is looking to run through the ACC with ease, and hopefully, that means we see plenty of NFL-caliber throws from Mensah that will make him the next transfer quarterback who impresses scouts this season.

Round 2, Pick 38: Samson Okunlola, OT, Miami

To build the future, you have to fortify the foundation, and that means Atlanta has to acquire a left tackle, so Jake Matthews can be the family man he deserves to be. Samson Okunlola's movement skills, especially his absurdly quick feet, are just one of his impressive traits that scouts will bet on if he comes out after this season. Okunlola's 6'6", 330-pound frame gives him such impressive size and he has experience playing inside as well.

Round 3, Pick 70: Tavion Gadson, DT, Kentucky

With Brandon Dorlus heading to the edge, the Falcons lose the interior pressure that Dorlus and, to a lesser extent, Ruke Orhorhoro brought on opposing quarterbacks. Tavion Gadson immediately brings that pass-rush juice back to the Falcons' line along with a knack for using his athleticism and size (6'4", 302 pounds) to stuff up the A-gaps.

Round 4, Pick 105: Niki Prongos, OT, Stanford

I couldn't help myself, and if Cunningham and Stefanski were met with the same choice, I don't think they would help themselves either. Niki Prongos hadn't started playing football until his senior year of high school, choosing to play baseball and basketball instead. Even in high school, he played tight end and defensive tackle alongside his duties at tackle. Prongos is such a fun athlete and would be a stellar pickup for Bill Callahan.

Round 5, Pick 179: Bruce Mitchell, C, BYU

#63 in white and blue has a case to be the best center in college football, and it would not surprise me if he finds a way into day two when it's all said and done. Mitchell has a stout anchor in pass protection alongside some strong hands in the run game. With this move, the Falcons would solve all three of their "problems" along the offensive line in one draft.

Round 6, Pick 216: Fluff Bothwell, RB, Mississippi State

Brian Robinson Jr. feels like a rental for this season, but the future of backing up Bijan Robinson can look like a running back like Fluff Bothwell. Don't let the name fool you; there is absolutely nothing soft about his game. Bothwell is 5'10", 230 pounds and, for a man of that size, he has impressive agility.

Round 7, Pick 220: Duce Robinson, WR, Florida State

KJ Duff is one of those players in the 2027 draft you wish had transferred to another team so he could get more eyes on his performance with a quarterback who can get him the ball. The same goes for Florida State receiver Duce Robinson. Robinson is 6'6", 230 pounds and has an incredibly large catch radius, while allowing Drake London to work more in the slot and Kyle Pitts over the middle of the field.

articles.body:

The 2026/2027 football season has kicked off, but week 1 isn't over without a little Sunday Night Football action. As it turns out, most NFL games are played on Sunday, and after a summer off from tailgating and Fantasy Football chats, this weekend's games are highly anticipated. On Sunday, September 13, catch games from the Kansas City Chiefs , Philadelphia Eagles , and more, and tune in for the first Sunday Night Football game of the season when the Dallas Cowboys and New York Giants attempt to win their first game of the season.

At a Glance: How to Watch Sunday Night Football

Streaming Options: SlingTV , Peacock , Hulu , Fubo , DIRECTV

Dates: 9/13, 9/20, 9/27, 10/4, 10/11, 10/18, 10/25, 11/1, 11/8, 11/15, 11/22, 11/26, 12/6, 12/13, 12/20, 12/27, 1/3/27

A lot of football is played on Sundays throughout the NFL season, but there's usually only one Sunday Night Football Game. The official time slot for Sunday Night Football game is 5:20 p.m. PT/8:20 ET , with teams alternating week to week. In the 2026/2027 season, there will be two Sunday Night Football games on November 26 (week 12): The Chiefs vs. Bills at 5:20 p.m. PT/8:20 ET and the Patriots vs. Chargers at 5:20 p.m. PT/8:20 ET.

There are several ways to tune into this weekend's Sunday Night Football kickoff, including some ways to watch for free. First up is SlingTV . Although it doesn't have any free trials, it's the cheapest way to watch Sunday Night Football, with a Sling 1 Day pass available for $4.99, a Sling 3 Day pass option for $9.99, or a full subscription starting at $45.99 per month. An even better option is the Sling Essentials & Select bundle ($34.99) which includes FOX News, ESPN, FS1, NFL Network, plus add on Sports Extra for access to NFL RedZone, FS2, SEC, ACC and more. If you're a mega-mega fan, consider the Season Pass bundle ($199+) which includes five months of Sling Essentials & Select + Sports Extra (which includes RedZone, ESPN channels, and NCAA conference networks like SEC, ACC, and Big Ten. Plus FOX One app access).

Hulu+ With Live TV includes a free three-day trial, plus free subscriptions to Hulu, Disney Plus, and ESPN Plus. If you subscribe to the regular Hulu subscription, you can upgrade and take advantage of this trial offer. After that, Hulu+ With Live TV plans go up to $89.99+ per month. DIRECTV offers a free five-day trial, then switches to a $89.99 per month plan after the trial ends (with $30 off your first month). Fubo has a free seven-day trial period before your selected plan (starting at $84.99) kicks in. Peacock doesn't offer a free trial, but there are workarounds if you have other subscription plans (more details below!).

How to Watch Sunday Night Football for Free With Sling: SlingTV does not offer free trials, but you can sign up for a Sling 1 Day pass for $4.99 or Sling 3 Day pass for $9.99. If you want to test the streaming platform out before committing to a monthly subscription. This is also a great alternative when you've already exhausted free trial options elsewhere (oops!).

SlingTV is our favorite (and the most affordable) way to watch Sunday Night Football because of its range of low-price offers. NBC, Fox, NFL RedZone, ESPN, ESPN2, and NFL Network, are also in select regions with Sling Blue and Sling Orange + Blue packages, which start at $45.99 per month.

Sling Essentials & Select bundle ($34.99) which includes FOX News, ESPN, FS1, NFL Network, plus add on Sports Extra for access to NFL RedZone, FS2, SEC, ACC and more.

Season Pass bundle ($199+) which includes five months of Sling Essentials & Select + Sports Extra (which includes RedZone, ESPN channels, and NCAA conference networks like SEC, ACC, and Big Ten. Plus FOX One app access).

Here's how to watch Sunday Night Football with Sling: Visit Sling.com/Service/Compare-Plans Click "Sign Up Now" Enter your information and payment method Search for Sunday Night Football and start watching

Our mission at SheKnows is to bring style to the people, and we only feature products we think you'll love as much as we do. SlingTV is a SheKnows sponsor, however, all products in this article were independently selected by our editors. Please note that if you purchase something by clicking on a link within this story, we may receive a small commission of the sale.

How to Watch Sunday Night Football for Free With Peacock: The Peacock app doesn't currently offer a free trial period, but there are some workarounds. If you're an Amazon Prime Member, you can add Peacock through Prime Video and access a 7-day free trial period. You can also sign up for a 30-day Walmart+ trial, which includes free access to Peacock.

Sunday Night Football airs on NBC and is available for streaming on Peacock with a Peacock Premium account. Through this subscription, you can watch live coverage of the games, as well as rewatch games, review game highlights, and more.

Here's how to watch Sunday Night Football with Peacock:

Visit peacocktv.com/sports/nfl Click "Get Started" Choose between the Premium and Premium Plus plans Enter your information and payment method Search for Sunday Night Football and start watching

How to Watch Sunday Night Football for Free With Hulu: If you want to watch Sunday Night Football for free, Hulu has you covered with a free three-day Hulu+ With Live TV trial. After that, you'll need to sign up for a subscription, and there are several options to choose from that are cheaper than many cable plans.

Hulu+ With Live TV is another way to watch Sunday Night Football, not just because it's available, but because you can get free subscriptions to Hulu, Disney Plus, and ESPN Plus when you sign up. Choose between a few plans, including a $89.99 per month ad-supported plan, which gets you Hulu + Live TV (with ads, access to 95+ channels, unlimited DVR, Disney+ (with ads), ESPN Select (with ads), and Hulu (with ads). An ad-free plan costs $99.99 per month, which offers Hulu (no ads), Disney+ (no ads), and ESPN Select (with ads) alongside Live TV.

How to watch Sunday Night Football with Hulu+ With Live TV:

Visit Hulu.com/liveTV Click "Sign Up Now" Enter your information and payment method Search for Sunday Night Football and start watching

How to Watch Sunday Night Football for Free With Fubo: If you've never signed up for Fubo before, you can get a seven day free trial (which is longer than Hulu and DIRECTV). Simply visit Fubo.TV and click the "Start for Free" button to sign up.

We love a streaming platform with options, and Fubo has them all . First, new customers can take advantage of the streaming platform's free seven-day trial period, which is longer than Hulu and DIRECTV. The streaming platform also offers three plans, including Pro for $84.99 per month, Elite for $94.99 per month, and Latino for $14.99 per month. Pro includes 180 channels, 1,000 hours of Cloud DVR, and the ability to watch on up to 10 screens at once. Elite includes everything in Pro, and a total of 256 channels and 4K resolution. Fubo's Latino plan offers Spanish-language TV at $14.99 per month.

How to watch Sunday Night Football with Fubu:

Visit Fubo.TV Click the "Start for Free" button Enter your information and payment method Search for Sunday Night Football and start watching

How to Watch Sunday Night Football for Free With DIRECTV: You can get a free five-day trial to DIRECTV when you sign up for one of the platform's three plans.

If you plan on watching more than football on Sundays, DIRECTV is a great choice with a free five-day trial period and excellent channel celetion. To access the trial period, you'll need to start up for a plan of your choice (if you cancel before the end of the trial, you won't get charged), including Entertainment for $89.99 per month, Choice for $94.99 per month, and Ultimate for $124.99 per month.

How to watch Sunday Night Football with DIRECTV:

Visit Directvstream.com/offers/packages Select "Start 5-day free trial" Choose the plan of your choice Enter your information and payment method Search for Sunday Night Football and start watching
